Plate with a hole in tension: Kirsch stress concentration

A plate with a central hole under uniaxial tension, checked against Kirsch's solution, Kt = 3. KoFEM's solid model gives Kt = 2.775 in the element next to the hole edge.

Open in KoFEM All examples

Model

Plate20,000 × 20,000 × 500 mm, modelled whole
HoleØ 2,000 mm, centred (d/W = 0.10)
MaterialSteel, linear elastic: E = 210,000 MPa, ν = 0.3
Fixedleft end face, Ux = Uy = Uz = 0 (34 nodes)
Loadright end face, P = 1.0 × 10⁹ N in +x as a uniform traction: σ = 100 MPa

Mesh

Elements768 linear hexahedra (CHEXA): 12 rings × 64 sectors × 1 layer
Nodes1,664
At the holefirst ring 62.5 mm deep, 98.2 mm long; the hole is a 64-sided polygon
Stressvon Mises per element, at the element centre

Results

Kt = peak von Mises / σKoFEMReferenceDifference
Kirsch, at the hole edge2.7753.000−7.5%
Kirsch, at the element centre (r = 1.030a, θ = 87.2°)2.7752.755+0.7%
Shell model, 1,536 CTRIA32.9393.000−2.0%

The peak element touches the hole, transverse to the load. Its centre is 30 mm from the edge, where Kirsch's stress has already fallen to 2.755σ; that, not the solve, is why the element value reads below 3.

Limitations

  • Linear elastic, small strain: no yielding at the hole.
  • Kt = 3 is for an infinite plate; a strip with d/W = 0.10 gives about 3.03 (Heywood).
  • One mesh, sampled at element centres: a finer first ring moves the value towards 3. Not a convergence study.
  • One element through the thickness: close to plane stress, no through-thickness variation.
  • A structured hex mesh from a script, not a Netgen mesh of STEP geometry, so it cannot be re-meshed in the app.

Reproduce

Open in KoFEM loads the solved model; Solve re-runs it in the browser with the same result. The model is defined in examples.mjs, this page is written by generate-plate-hole-page.mjs.

References

  1. G. Kirsch, “Die Theorie der Elastizität und die Bedürfnisse der Festigkeitslehre”, Zeitschrift des Vereines deutscher Ingenieure 42 (1898), 797–807.
  2. R. B. Heywood, Designing by Photoelasticity, Chapman & Hall, 1952.
